mainEntity.name: How much does a daily commute cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on distance, vehicle, fuel price, tolls and parking. A 37-mile round trip in a 28.5 MPG car with $3.55 gas costs about $4.60 in fuel per day, more when wear, tolls and parking are included. Enter your numbers above for an exact figure.

mainEntity.name: Should I use the IRS mileage rate?

acceptedAnswer.text: The IRS business rate is designed to cover the full running cost of a vehicle, including depreciation and insurance, so it gives a higher and more complete per-mile figure than fuel alone. Note that it is a tax rate for business travel, and commuting from home to a regular workplace is generally not deductible.

mainEntity.name: Is my commute time worth counting?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is not a cash cost, but it is a real trade-off. Valuing an hour of your time at a fraction of your wage shows what a shorter commute or a remote day is worth. Turn the option off to see cash costs only.

mainEntity.name: How is an electric vehicle handled?

acceptedAnswer.text: Switch to Electric and enter miles per kWh and your price per kWh. Energy cost per mile is price divided by miles per kWh, and wear and other costs work as before.

mainEntity.name: When is transit cheaper than driving?

acceptedAnswer.text: When a monthly pass costs less than your monthly driving cost, including parking and tolls. The comparison panel shows the difference, and parking charges are usually what tips it.

mainEntity.name: How do I calculate my commute cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Round-trip miles × days × (fuel price ÷ MPG + wear per mile), plus tolls and parking for each day. At 18.5 miles each way, 28.5 MPG, $3.55 gas and $0.092 wear that is about $160.26 a month before tolls and parking.

mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to commute 20 miles each way?

acceptedAnswer.text: At 28.5 MPG, $3.55 gas and $0.092 wear, fuel and wear come to about $2,079 a year over 240 days. At the IRS rate of 76 cents a mile it is $7,296.

mainEntity.name: What is the AAA cost per mile to drive?

acceptedAnswer.text: AAA's 2026 Your Driving Costs study puts the average new vehicle at $12,863 a year, or about 86 cents a mile at 15,000 miles, including depreciation, insurance and finance charges. Fuel is 17.3 cents of that and maintenance, repairs and tires 11.7 cents.

mainEntity.name: Should I use the AAA rate, the IRS rate or fuel only?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fuel only shows the cash you spend each trip. The IRS rate (76 cents from 1 July 2026) and AAA's all-in figure also count depreciation and insurance, which matter if the commute adds miles to a car you would otherwise barely drive.

mainEntity.name: How many hours a year do I spend commuting?

acceptedAnswer.text: One-way minutes × 8 for a 5-day week over 48 weeks. A 45-minute commute is 360 hours a year, or 9 forty-hour working weeks.
Under 29 CFR 785.35, normal travel from home to work is not worktime. Travel between work sites during the day can be treated differently.
Generally no. The IRS treats travel between home and a regular workplace as personal. Check IRS guidance or a tax adviser for your situation.

mainEntity.name: What is the 2026 limit for pre-tax commuter benefits?

acceptedAnswer.text: $340 a month for transit and vanpool combined and $340 a month for parking. Your employer must offer the benefit.

mainEntity.name: Is a long commute worth a higher salary?

acceptedAnswer.text: Subtract the extra fuel and wear from the extra pay, then divide by the extra hours. In the example above $6,000 more pay leaves about $3,921 for 240 extra hours, roughly $16.34 an hour.
